findings.where: The full-width blue 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' band with its Subscribe button, right under the first screen (desktop-02 top; phone-01, straight after the address)
findings.fault: A second call to action, as large as the first, comes right after the one personal way to reach Mark. It talks about him as 'Mark's' when the hero just spoke in his own voice. It offers a product, 'briefings on PPP reform', that nothing in the brief says he provides. And the button goes to #subscribe, which matches nothing on the page, so a visitor who clicks it gets nothing. On a phone the band takes a full screen of the page, straight after the address.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one message and one action and rules out anything salesy or in a firm's voice. The development-bank officer, who is promised a subscription that doesn't exist. Mark, because 'briefings' is a claim he never made.

findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph (desktop-01 right; phone-01 top)
findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of him speaking. What's built is a cut-out head and shoulders on a flat slate ground. The lectern, the event and the room are keyed away, so nothing shows him working or invited to speak. It reads as a headshot pasted onto a background, and the rough keyed edge around his hair makes it look cheap. That is the 'slick' look the research warns against.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked v7 for Mark seen speaking. A procurement reader who wants to judge his standing from a photo at a named event, and here gets an anonymous cut-out.

findings.where: First screen, next to the 'Write to me directly' action
findings.fault: Next to the action there is nothing to show this person has done the work: no named body that asked him, no region or country of his work, no recent talk with its venue. The lede says who he advises but gives no evidence, and the base country or region is missing everywhere on the page, footer included. The visitor has to take him on trust or go to LinkedIn.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank or agency officer checking whether he has done this kind of work in their region before writing. First-visit trust items 3, 6 and 14 apply to a solo advisor.

findings.where: First screen, the heading 'In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of Public-Private Partnerships.'
findings.fault: The heading promises a view about a turning point, but nothing on the page says what the turning point is or links to where Mark argues it. A reader who is curious about the claim has nowhere to go except the email address.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who is intrigued and wants to read Mark's case before writing to a stranger. A promise with no follow-through reads as a slogan, not a view.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' lecture card (desktop-06; phone-04)
findings.fault: The lecture card gives a type and a date, but not where it was given or who hosted it, which is the most persuasive fact a talk carries.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who judges standing by who invited the speaker (feel the CV: the newest talk with its venue).
